CHOICE: 3
CONFIDENCE: 3

Solution 3 is the only one with a checkable lower bound. Its construction has $|X| = s-1$ and $|C| = k+s-2$, with edges that meet both $X$ and $C$ plus all $k$-subsets of $C$. I checked that the matching number is $s-1$ and that all $k+2s-3$ vertices in $X \cup C$ exceed the threshold, so $m \ge k+2s-2$. The $k=2$ and $s=2$ cases agree with direct checks. Solution 1 ($ks$) would need $ks-1$ high-degree vertices, which seems to exceed what is achievable when $k \ge 3$. Solution 2 agrees with Solution 3 at $k=2$ and $s=2$ but diverges for $k,s\ge3$ (e.g. $k=s=3$: 8 vs 7), and it gives no construction. I did not prove the matching upper bound in general, so confidence is moderate.
